clue.text: Favourite grace said in tumultuous seas

definitions.meaning: a favourite person is a beloved one, a pet or sweetheart
points to Grace ..., the lighthouse keeper's daughter who rowed out through a storm in 1838 to rescue shipwrecked sailors

explanation.surface: A favourite prayer is said before a meal while the sea rages outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grace' looks like a prayer before a meal, but it is a first name: Grace Darling is a Victorian British heroine of a sea rescue off Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: A beloved person is called a sweetheart, and the famous heroine of the 1838 storm rescue bore this surname.

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
requests as a verb means asks

explanation.surface: A mother asks for clothes made of fabric that can be worn either way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven cloth whose design shows on both faces, so it can be used either side out.

clue.text: This journalism is bang on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another comes after it, so the time follows the bang

parts.note: a bang is a loud noise, a report like a gunshot
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Praise for a piece of journalism that is exactly right and punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bang on time' reads as 'punctual', but 'bang' is a gunshot's noise and 'on' only stacks the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is the reporting of news by journalists, a kind of journalism.

indicators.note: the answer is taken out from within the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Coal dust and waste taken from a miner who is digging a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slack' is also coal dust, which fits the mining picture, but here it means sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slack lacks energy or movement, which is the sense of an inactive, motionless thing.

clue.text: Oral examination could reveal value of present hunter, for example

definitions.text: Oral examination could reveal value of present hunter, for example

parts.words: Oral examination could reveal value of present hunter, for example
parts.note: a horse's age and worth are judged by its teeth; the proverb warns against looking into the mouth of a horse given as a present, and a hunter is a kind of horse

explanation.surface: A spoken exam might show how good today's hunter is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral examination' suggests a viva; it is looking into a horse's mouth. A hunter is a horse ridden for foxhunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says not to inspect a present animal's teeth, so the answer is a horse received as a present.

clue.text: Animal with the most superior brain

definitions.text: Animal with the most superior brain

parts.words: Animal with the most superior brain
parts.note: superior is read literally as highest up: the tallest creature carries its brain higher than any other

explanation.surface: A claim about which creature is the cleverest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' suggests intelligence, but it means physically highest.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked African creature is the tallest living land mammal, so its brain sits highest.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Breed of mastermind' with no letter count; it looks cut short (GENIUS less I needs a word for the removal), and no search found the full printed text

parts.note: to harvest crops is to reap them
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: A farmer reports that crops are growing back and orders the fruit picked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crops up' looks like more harvest talk, but it is the idiom for 'turns up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up once more is to come back into view after an absence.

definitions.meaning: a soft sugary confection made with butter and milk
an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish

explanation.surface: A dismissal of some sugary talk as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a soft toffee-like confection and is also an old exclamation meaning rubbish or humbug.

indicators.note: the word reported is a spoken one, so the novelist's first name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Hemingway's first name is Ernest

explanation.surface: Hemingway's grave, as told by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective for solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave manner is serious and sincere.

indicators.note: something hearted has a heart put in, so the soft letter goes into the middle of the man

parts.note: a man is a male
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A gentle-hearted man who turns sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft-hearted' looks like kindly, but splits into P (soft) placed in the heart of MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar species of this tree yields a sweet sap boiled down into syrup.

clue.text: Sibelius, for example, fellow not near coast

parts.note: someone living away from the coast is an inlander

explanation.surface: Sibelius described as a man who lived far from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Sibelius, the composer, was a native of Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibelius was a national of the Nordic country of Finland, so he is an example of its people.

definitions.meaning: small wounds or nicks on the skin
grazes, or the act of rubbing roughly

explanation.surface: Minor injuries: nicks and grazes.
explanation.definitionFit: Light marks made by claws or thorns are both shallow cuts and surface grazes.

definitions.meaning: a part or portion of a larger thing
a single painting, sculpture or composition

explanation.surface: A close-up section of a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a portion of a whole and also an individual artistic creation, as in a museum item.

clue.text: Features of ship lined with pitch?

indicators.note: a thing lined with something has it inside, so the pitch goes within the ship

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
pitch is tar, used to seal a ship's seams

explanation.surface: Asks what a boat's hull, sealed with pitch, looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' reads as parts of a ship; it is the verb, as a film features or headlines its leading actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A film that features an actor gives them the leading role, which is to headline it.

parts.note: flags are paving stones; the paved walkways beside a US street are laid with them

explanation.surface: Someone hails a taxi on a street in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags down' suggests hailing a cab, but flags are flagstones laid down in paving.
explanation.definitionFit: The American name for pavements along a street, which are paved with stone slabs.

clue.text: Special treatment for favourite at Cleveland racecourse

indicators.note: the favourite is placed at the course, so it is attached after it

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in Cleveland, in north-east England, with a horse racecourse
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Treating the favourite horse specially at a northern racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favourite' suggests a racehorse at the course; here it is just PET.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson strip laid out for dignitaries stands for lavish, ceremonious hospitality.

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters of the preceding word are formed anew

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
mites are tiny parasites

explanation.surface: Describes outdated parasites shaped like rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one word meaning dated; split it, 'fashioned' rearranges OLD into DOL.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a mountain range in north-eastern Italy, part of the Alps.

clue.text: Writer of English in sacerdotal clothing?

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so the priestly word goes around the English letter

parts.note: sacerdotal means relating to priests, priestly

explanation.surface: Asks for a writer of English who wears priestly vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacerdotal clothing' suggests vestments; 'clothing' is the container. J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: J. B. Priestley was an English author of plays and novels such as An Inspector Calls.

indicators.note: the agreeable word follows, coming after the drug

parts.note: speed is a slang name for amphetamine
well, as in 'all is well', means fine or satisfactory

explanation.surface: Veronica is feeling fine after taking amphetamine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name; it is the botanical name of a plant genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the genus name of a small blue-flowered garden plant.

definitions.meaning: to down a drink is to gulp it

explanation.surface: Soft feathers taken from a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like feathers; it is the verb to gulp.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to gulp food or drink and names a fork-tailed summer migrant bird.

definitions.meaning: a thin strip of wood or paper used to carry a flame
a tumble, especially from a horse or bicycle

explanation.surface: A lighter tumbles to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a taper of wood or paper for lighting fires and also a tumble.

indicators.note: sailors pronounce the nautical word as a sound like the clue's first word, so this is how it is said

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors say they were tempted towards a sheltered spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors pronounce the word as 'loo-erd', which sounds like 'lured'.
explanation.definitionFit: The side sheltered from the wind is the lee, so this means on or towards the sheltered side.

clue.text: Quarrel as school fails to open

indicators.note: the school's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out because a school does not open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' looks like an argument; it is a crossbow bolt. Harrow is a well-known boarding school in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is the bolt shot from a crossbow, a short missile like an archer's.

clue.text: Large blackbird heard in storm over the north

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another sits above it, so the storm word comes first

parts.note: to storm in anger is to rave
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A big dark bird can be heard in a storm above the northern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard in' only joins the definition to the wordplay; nothing here is a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: This large black bird of the crow family is far bigger than the songbird of the same colour.

clue.text: So much coffee is steamed badly

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Coffee is steamed poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ISSTEAMED. 'So much coffee' means the quantity held by one small cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A small after-dinner cup holds a measure of strong black coffee, so its name stands for that amount.

indicators.note: the king is held inside the beloved

parts.note: a beloved person is dear
R (rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A gloomy king is hugged by his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning gloomy or dismal.

clue.text: Pole to carry this ritual object

definitions.text: Pole to carry this ritual object

parts.words: Pole to carry this ritual object
parts.note: a tall carved pole of North American peoples carries figures of this sacred emblem, so the pole is named after it

explanation.surface: A pole made to bear a sacred object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality; it is a tall carved post.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred emblem of a clan or tribe, carved on the tall posts of Pacific north-west peoples.

clue.text: The most delightful passion settles with time

parts.note: love is passion
dust settles or lies on a surface

explanation.surface: The finest passion calms down as time goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles' suggests calming; here it means rests, as dust lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of lovely means most charming or attractive.

clue.text: City in Oklahoma has a piece of baggage returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: baggage is an old disparaging word for an immoral woman, as is slut

explanation.surface: An Oklahoma city gets a lost suitcase sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of baggage' suggests luggage; it is the dated insult for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is the second-largest city of the US state of Oklahoma.

clue.text: One could win at Cruft's — someday, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible arrangement of the word's letters

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to win at the dog show one day.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's leading dog show. 'perhaps' rearranges SOMEDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: This white Siberian spitz breed is a pedigree dog that could take a prize at a show.
